items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.one_liner: A Check Point vulnerability is now confirmed to be under active exploitation, requiring immediate patching.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-123039, an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability in multiple Check Point products, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. This addition mandates that Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies prioritize remediation of this flaw on publicly exposed assets. The vulnerability allows for potential total control of the asset post-exploitation. CISA continues to urge all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management by prioritizing KEV-listed items.
items.bottom_line: Federal agencies and private organizations must prioritize patching CVE-2026-123039 to prevent attackers from gaining full control of Check Point assets.

claims.support_span: CVE-2026-123039 Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: CVSS 9.2, remote code execution via OOM longjmp
CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

claims.text: CVE-2026-109618 involves a remote code execution vulnerability where handling out-of-memory errors via longjmp() leaves request memory uninitialized due to improper control flow management, allowing attackers to reliably achieve RCE using out-of-memory (OOM) triggers.
claims.support_span: CVE-2026-109618 involves a remote code execution vulnerability where handling out-of-memory errors via longjmp() leaves request memory uninitialized due to improper control flow management, allowing attackers to reliably achieve RCE using out-of-memory (OOM) triggers.

claims.text: Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet.

items.title: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical command injection flaw in UnrealIRCd is being actively exploited, requiring immediate remediation.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-114713, an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability in UnrealIRCd, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. The flaw allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands, which are then executed with server authority. Federal agencies are required to apply mitigations by November 16, 2026. This vulnerability poses a significant risk of unauthorized command execution across linked IRC infrastructure.
items.bottom_line: Organizations running UnrealIRCd must patch CVE-2026-114713 immediately to prevent unauthorized users from executing commands with full server authority.

items.title: ZDI-26-964: (Pwn2Own) Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol chacha20_decrypt Integer Underflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE in Philips Hue Bridge allows nearby attackers to compromise the smart home hub.
items.summary: A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been disclosed in the Philips Hue Bridge, affecting the HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP) service. The flaw, discovered during Pwn2Own, is an integer underflow that occurs when the service parses pairing requests on TCP port 8080. Network-adjacent attackers can exploit this without authentication to execute arbitrary code on the device. A fix has been released in Bridge v2 software version 1975170000.
items.bottom_line: Users of Philips Hue Bridge must update to version 1975170000 immediately to mitigate an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability.

claims.text: The vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code without authentication.
claims.support_span: This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

claims.text: The flaw is an integer underflow in the HomeKit Accessory Protocol service.
claims.support_span: The specific flaw exists within the HomeKit Accessory Protocol service, which listens on TCP port 8080 by default. When parsing pairing requests, the process does not properly validate user-supplied data, which can result in an integer underflow

When chained together, these flaws allow unauthenticated remote attackers to achieve command execution at the root level. Barracuda released specific patches—designated Patch-1 and Patch-2—to resolve these issues in version 9.4.0.029. The analysis underscores the ongoing risk posed by edge devices that inspect incoming mail with high privileges.

items.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage as it reports broad recovery
items.one_liner: A massive global outage highlights the fragility of enterprise reliance on single-provider cloud ecosystems.
items.summary: A global Microsoft service outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, and other 365 products for over 24 hours, affecting 430 million users across 70 countries. The company attributed the incident to a technical issue during a network capacity upgrade rather than a cyberattack. Impact was widespread, hitting government agencies, hospitals, schools, and businesses in North America, Europe, and Asia. While services began recovering by Friday afternoon, Microsoft has not provided a timeline for full restoration.

The fixes include a critical integer overflow in the regular expression compiler, high-severity issues in OAuth/OIDC discovery and OmniAuth-to-LDAP auto-linking, and several medium and low severity bugs. Installations not using official packages with bundled runtimes must also upgrade Ruby to version 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later to mitigate CVE-2026-110264. items.title: CVE-2026-119618: What We Know About the Critical Apache mod_http2 Race Condition
items.one_liner: Critical HTTP/2 race condition CVE-2026-119618 in Apache allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
items.summary: The Apache Software Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-119618, a critical race condition in the mod_http2 module affecting Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The flaw arises from improper synchronization in the assign_headers() function, leading to heap memory corruption and potential unauthenticated remote code execution. Red Hat reports that public research has demonstrated reliable exploitation against default configurations. The issue is resolved in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71.

items.title: US flights resume after FAA lifts hours-long nationwide ground stop

items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) enforced a nationwide ground stop halting all US departing flights for over four hours due to a temporary telecommunications outage impacting all 22 air route traffic control centres. The suspension caused widespread travel chaos, resulting in over 4,000 flight cancellations and more than 10,000 delays before operations resumed. Federal officials confirmed there was no indication of a security threat or cyberattack, while investigators examined potential software update issues. Air Space Intelligence explicitly denied that its newly deployed AI-powered SMART management system caused the failure.

items.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
items.one_liner: SilentAir exploited hacked telecom equipment in Asia using SS7 and Diameter signaling to intercept 2FA codes.
items.summary: A state-level spying group named SilentAir hacked equipment inside mobile operators across at least six Asian countries to intercept SMS 2FA codes and calls, primarily targeting individuals in Taiwan. Security firm Enea discovered that the attackers exploited SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols by sending fraudulent UpdateLocation messages via compromised IPX network infrastructure. The operations occurred in intermittent bursts since early 2025 and targeted various government and political VIPs. Enea has notified the affected operators, though it remains unclear whether the compromised equipment has been cleaned.

items.title: AI Pentest Tool AntiFox Abused To Steal AWS Credentials
items.one_liner: The open-source AntiFox agentic framework is being weaponized to automate rapid, multi-stage attacks against cloud infrastructure and web servers.
items.summary: Attackers are increasingly leveraging AntiFox, an open-source, Chinese-language agentic penetration testing framework, to automate attacks against IIS servers and AWS environments. The tool chains exploitation steps, such as web shell deployment on IIS or rapid enumeration of AWS IAM roles and services, with minimal human intervention. Arctic Wolf Labs observed the framework being used to exfiltrate configuration files, database credentials, and sensitive secrets from production environments. This shift highlights how agentic AI tools are lowering the barrier for attackers to perform consistent, high-speed reconnaissance and exploitation.

items.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
items.one_liner: A major international police operation has disrupted three significant malware families and seized millions of stolen credentials.
items.summary: Operation Endgame, an international law enforcement effort, has successfully dismantled infrastructure for Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware. Police seized 235 servers and 257 domains, recovering approximately 6.4 million stolen login credentials from over 40,000 victims. Gootloader, which used SEO poisoning on hacked WordPress sites to deliver ransomware, is estimated to have infected millions of computers since 2020. While no arrests were announced, the operation also shut down the 'Virtualine/Omegatech' bulletproof hosting service used by the StealC infostealer.
items.bottom_line: The takedown of Gootloader and StealC infrastructure significantly disrupts the initial access broker market, though victims should still check for compromised credentials.

items.title: Maersk Reveals Data Breach as Extortion Group Demands $5m
items.one_liner: A legacy system breach at Maersk highlights the persistent security risks inherent in M&A activity and inherited infrastructure.
items.summary: Shipping giant Maersk has confirmed a data breach after the WhiteArmor extortion group claimed to have stolen 100GB of data. The incident involved a legacy system from a previous acquisition and allegedly includes driver records, plaintext passwords, and mobile device logs. WhiteArmor is demanding a $5 million ransom in Bitcoin and has recently targeted other logistics firms like J.B. Hunt and Ryder. Maersk states that no sensitive data has been disclosed and customer platforms remain operational.
items.bottom_line: Maersk's breach by the WhiteArmor group serves as a warning that legacy systems from acquisitions remain high-value targets for data-theft extortionists.

items.summary: Vanderbilt University is progressively restoring campus systems online following a cyberattack claimed by the BYOD ransomware group. items.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen

items.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
items.one_liner: Analyze the geopolitical and regulatory fallout surrounding Nvidia's chip distribution hubs following executive resignation and export control probes.
items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped down from the company following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, the executive running Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed. Megaspeed became a top buyer of Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia and is currently under investigation by Singaporean authorities for suspected fraudulent export declarations and illicitly routing advanced US semiconductors to Chinese buyers in violation of export controls. items.title: Cisco BroadWorks Out-of-Band Blind XML External Entity Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical XML external entity injection vulnerability in Cisco BroadWorks allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate sensitive configuration files.
items.summary: Cisco BroadWorks contains a critical vulnerability in its Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser that allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to read sensitive configuration files. The flaw stems from improper parsing where external entity resolution is enabled by default. Attackers can exploit this by sending a crafted XML message to the OCI-P service, potentially gaining access to sensitive filesystem data. Cisco has released software updates to address this issue, and there are no available workarounds.
key_facts: Affected: Cisco BroadWorks OCI XML Parser
items.bottom_line: Organizations running Cisco BroadWorks must apply the latest software updates immediately to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive system configurations.

items.title: ZDI-26-1002: Linux Kernel Net Scheduler Qdisc Improper Validation of Array Index Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A Linux kernel array index validation flaw in taprio_enqueue allows local attackers to achieve privilege escalation.
items.summary: A local privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the Linux Kernel Net Scheduler Qdisc due to improper validation of array indexes in the taprio_enqueue function. A low-privileged local attacker can exploit the lack of proper bounds checking to trigger a write past the end of an allocated array, allowing them to execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel. Linux has released an upstream code commit to resolve the flaw.
key_facts: Affected Component: taprio_enqueue function in Linux Kernel Net Scheduler Qdisc
items.bottom_line: Local attackers can exploit a bounds-checking vulnerability in the Linux net scheduler to achieve root privilege escalation.

items.one_liner: An uninitialized resource vulnerability in the Linux kernel KSMBD server allows unauthenticated remote attackers to leak sensitive information.
items.summary: An unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability exists in the Linux Kernel KSMBD component within the ksmbd_conn_handler_loop function. items.title: CVE-2026-123039: Check Point Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA has mandated the patching of a root-level privilege escalation vulnerability in Check Point security products.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-123039 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, highlighting an incorrect permission assignment in multiple Check Point products. The vulnerability exists in the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon, which listens on a world-writable local socket without authentication. An authenticated local user can exploit this to execute commands with root privileges. Federal agencies are required to apply vendor-provided mitigations by November 16, 2026, to comply with binding operational directives.
items.bottom_line: The inclusion of CVE-2026-123039 in the CISA KEV catalog confirms active exploitation and necessitates immediate remediation for all affected Check Point gateways and management servers.

items.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
items.one_liner: Google's new Gemini Decisions API enables ultra-fast, cost-effective closed-set multimodal decision making without generative token billing.
items.summary: Google has introduced the Gemini Decisions API powered by the new Gemini Decision 1 model, designed for fast, closed-set multimodal choices such as tool selection, model routing, and policy checks. The model processes multimodal inputs across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs alongside up to 1,000 independent questions in a single forward pass without token-by-token text generation. It delivers an end-to-end latency of 150 to 250 ms at a cost of $0.10 per 1 million input tokens with zero output tokens billed.

items.one_liner: A major GitHub supply-chain attack compromises nearly 4,837 accounts, injecting credential-stealing payloads into thousands of code repositories.
items.summary: Attackers hijacked 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a secret stealer payload into software repositories via CI workflows and malicious commits, according to security researchers at Aikido Security and SafeDep. The malicious workflow updates targeted cloud credentials, repository secrets, and developer systems via npm postinstall hooks across more than 8,000 repositories. Security researchers advise affected repository owners to immediately revoke all commit tokens, SSH keys, and OAuth grants, and to rotate all exposed secrets.
items.bottom_line: Developers must immediately rotate all repository secrets, cloud credentials, and commit tokens if their repositories received malicious workflow commits.

items.title: Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed
items.one_liner: A newly disclosed iOS sandbox escape ('worse_query') exposes crypto wallet keys to sideloaded apps; update devices and remove untrusted apps.
items.summary: Binance issued a security warning regarding an iOS sandbox escape published on GitHub under the name 'worse_query' that permits an app to read other applications' data files on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27. Developed by researcher forcequit in collaboration with 0xjohnny, the exploit relies on an App Group container created via sideloading tools such as AltStore and SideStore (demonstrated in apps like WQ Files by Christoph Kolbicz) to access app containers without a jailbreak. Apple released iOS fixes for other components yesterday, but no patch for the sandbox escape has been confirmed. Binance advised users to delete untrusted sideloaded apps, update their software, and secure their crypto wallet keys.
items.bottom_line: A public iOS sandbox escape ('worse_query') allows sideloaded apps to access other applications' files, posing risks to cryptocurrency private keys.

items.one_liner: Newly disclosed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell flaws in N-able N-central enable root and SYSTEM RCE on patched servers.
items.summary: Security researcher Sean Bales disclosed new proof-of-concept exploits codenamed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell targeting N-able N-central on-premise version 2026.4 HF2. items.title: On the hunt for ARTEX: understanding agentic attacks in AWS environments
items.one_liner: AI-native penetration framework ARTEX was observed actively exploiting compromised AWS credentials and public Cognito pools to hunt for financial data.
items.summary: Datadog Security Labs reported in-the-wild activity by ARTEX—an AI-native autonomous penetration framework developed by a Chinese creator—targeting AWS environments to harvest financial data and credentials in October 2026. Operating through hosted web consoles and LLM agent teams, ARTEX utilizes compromised long-term IAM access keys to search CloudWatch logs via FilterLogEvents and abuses public Amazon Cognito user pools for anonymous sign-ups and account enumeration. Originally published on GitHub in July 2026 and closed-source after surpassing 12,000 forks, the platform accepts API keys for multiple LLM providers such as OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Anthropic, dynamically switching providers if keys are revoked.

items.title: CVE-2026-82504 - VITEC EZ TV Platform Server Unauthenticated File Upload via UploadHandler.ashx
items.one_liner: Upgrade VITEC EZ TV Platform Server to version 8.5.0+ to prevent unauthenticated RCE via CVE-2026-82504.
items.summary: An unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability, designated as CVE-2026-82504, affects VITEC EZ TV Platform Server prior to version 8.5.0. Attackers can leverage the upload handler script via the X-FILENAME HTTP request header to upload malicious ASPX files directly to the web-accessible directory without authentication. Because the server immediately executes these files, remote code execution is achieved within the context of the web server process. Patches have been issued for versions 8.3.0 through 8.4.1, and users are urged to upgrade to 8.5.0 or later.

items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-82504 enables unauthenticated remote code execution via arbitrary file uploads on unpatched VITEC EZ TV Platform Servers.

items.title: CVE-2026-128132 - AIOHTTP: WebSocket receive queue limits bypassed by small or compressed messages
items.one_liner: AIOHTTP WebSocket queue limits can be bypassed, leading to memory exhaustion via compressed messages.
items.summary: AIOHTTP versions prior to 3.14.4 are vulnerable to a WebSocket receive queue bypass. The reader continues to parse frames even after the receive queue pauses, and empty messages are not correctly accounted for in queue size limits. Additionally, compressed messages can expand significantly, allowing a remote peer to overwhelm server or client memory. This issue is resolved in version 3.14.4.
items.bottom_line: Update AIOHTTP to 3.14.4 to prevent remote attackers from causing memory exhaustion through WebSocket message manipulation.

claims.text: A remote peer can send many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them and cause excessive memory use in a server or client.

items.title: CVE-2026-128131 - AIOHTTP: Concatenated compressed streams cause excessive CPU use
items.one_liner: A critical DoS vulnerability in AIOHTTP allows remote attackers to block event loops via crafted compressed payloads.
items.summary: AIOHTTP versions prior to 3.14.4 are vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack caused by quadratic CPU usage during the decompression of concatenated streams. A remote attacker can send a crafted request body or WebSocket message to block the server's event loop. This issue is caused by the framework passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor for each member of a payload. Users are advised to upgrade to version 3.14.4 to mitigate this vulnerability.
key_facts: Impact: Denial of Service (Event loop blocking)
items.bottom_line: If you use AIOHTTP in your Python stack, you must update to 3.14.4 immediately to prevent event loop exhaustion.

claims.text: Prior to 3.14.4, aiohttp decompresses each member of a payload containing many concatenated gzip, deflate, or zstd streams by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, causing quadratic CPU use.

items.title: CVE-2026-128130 - AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade
items.one_liner: A critical memory exhaustion vulnerability in AIOHTTP's pure-Python parser requires an immediate update to version 3.14.4.
items.summary: AIOHTTP versions prior to 3.14.4 contain a vulnerability where the pure-Python parser incorrectly handles request remainders after a declined upgrade. When the pipelined request queue is full, the parser feeds the unparsed data back to the caller, causing the internal buffer to grow uncontrollably with each request. This flaw can lead to excessive memory consumption and repeated processing of already-handled requests. Users are advised to upgrade to version 3.14.4 to mitigate this issue.
items.bottom_line: If you are running AIOHTTP without C-extensions, you are vulnerable to memory-based DoS attacks and must patch to 3.14.4.

claims.text: The issue affects deployments using AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS or otherwise running without the standard C-extension wheel, and can cause excessive memory use and repeated request processing.

items.summary: Apache APISIX is vulnerable to an authentication bypass due to a path normalization mismatch between routing and upstream forwarding. An unauthenticated client can access protected upstream paths if a route without authentication exists on the same upstream and the upstream does not collapse encoded dot segments. This affects versions 0.9 through 3.19.0 and is fixed in version 3.20.0.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can bypass route-level authentication in Apache APISIX by exploiting path normalization discrepancies.

items.summary: Apache APISIX is vulnerable to an authentication bypass via identity header spoofing in its jwe-decrypt and forward-auth configurations. When configured with specific permissive settings (strict: false or allow_degradation: true), an unauthenticated client can supply their own identity values that the upstream treats as trusted. This affects versions 3.18.0 through 3.19.0 and is fixed in version 3.20.0.
items.bottom_line: Permissive configurations in Apache APISIX's authentication plugins allow unauthenticated users to spoof identity headers.

items.title: Dropbear: the restriction names an address — permitopen/permitlisten not enforced for unix-socket forwarding, docker.sock reachable (HEAD 99baf182, live-proven)
items.one_liner: Your restricted SSH keys for Dropbear are currently ineffective against Unix-socket forwarding, potentially exposing your Docker daemon.
items.summary: The Dropbear SSH server fails to enforce per-destination restrictions for Unix-socket forwarding, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive sockets like docker.sock. While TCP forwarding correctly respects permitopen and permitlisten restrictions, the streamlocal forwarding implementation lacks these checks entirely. This vulnerability exists in current versions, including commit 99baf182, and remains unpatched despite previous attempts to secure the path. Administrators relying on Dropbear for restricted access should be aware that Unix-socket forwarding bypasses intended security boundaries.
key_facts: Impact: Unauthorized access to local sockets like docker.sock
items.bottom_line: Dropbear's Unix-socket forwarding ignores permitopen/permitlisten restrictions, allowing unauthorized access to local sockets.

claims.text: A unix socket is not an address, and on the socket path the restriction is never consulted.
claims.support_span: A unix socket is not an address, and on the socket path the restriction is never consulted.

claims.text: The per-destination restrictions — the other half of what that title announces — were not applied.

items.title: Open WebUI: the Windows installer mints the master key from the install second — CVE-2025-15603 was rejected; here is the measurement
items.one_liner: Open WebUI's Windows installer uses a weak, predictable seed for its master secret key, allowing full session token forgery.
items.summary: The Windows installer for Open WebUI generates a master secret key using a linear congruential generator seeded only by the installation time in seconds. This flaw allows an attacker to recover the master key in approximately 2.1 seconds, enabling the forgery of administrator session tokens. Despite being reported as CVE-2025-15603, the vendor disputed the finding and rejected the CVE, claiming no action was required. New research confirms the vulnerability persists across all 178 release tags, with most lacking even basic per-account session stamps.
key_facts: Vulnerability: Predictable master secret key generation
items.bottom_line: Administrators should assume all Open WebUI installations on Windows are compromised and rotate all secrets immediately.

claims.text: Open WebUI's Windows installer (start_windows.bat) generates WEBUI_SECRET_KEY — the master secret that signs every session token — from the C library's rand(), a linear congruential generator seeded once with the current time in seconds.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.one_liner: LLMON is an XML-like markup language designed to defeat prompt injection and replace brittle JSON parsing in LLMs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced LLMON (LLM Object Notation), an LLM-native markup language designed to replace JSON for causal language models by using reserved special-token delimiters for explicit structure and data binding. By wrapping semantic components in tags and mapping unique identifiers to instructions, the format prevents indirect prompt injections and stops models from pulling unrelated context into answers. IBM has released two experimental preview models based on Granite 4.1 (3B and 8B parameters) trained natively on LLMON, alongside a GitHub toolkit for conversions and workflows.
items.bottom_line: Adopting LLMON and its supporting Granite models eliminates indirect prompt injection risks by explicitly binding instructions to data payloads.

claims.text: To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models.

items.one_liner: A NULL pointer dereference in MP4Box allows attackers to crash the application via malicious XMT files.
items.summary: GPAC's MP4Box utility is vulnerable to a NULL pointer dereference when processing crafted XMT input files. items.title: CVE-2026-62976 - BACnet Stack: Consecutive AtomicWriteFile(record-access) appends can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read in the RAMFS file backend
items.one_liner: If you maintain embedded systems using BACnet Stack, update to version 1.5.1 or 1.6.0 to prevent potential heap memory corruption.
items.summary: A heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the BACnet Stack open-source protocol library due to flawed record-counting logic in the RAMFS file backend. Specifically, consecutive AtomicWriteFile append requests cause the system to incorrectly calculate buffer lengths, leading to memory access past the allocated heap. This vulnerability affects versions prior to 1.5.1 and has been addressed in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.
key_facts: Affected: BACnet Stack versions prior to 1.5.1
items.bottom_line: Embedded systems using older versions of the BACnet Stack are vulnerable to memory corruption via crafted AtomicWriteFile requests.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: When One GPU Isn’t Enough: Serving GLM-5.3 Across Two NVIDIA DGX Stations with vLLM

items.summary: This technical guide details how to serve the 753-billion-parameter GLM-5.3 model across two NVIDIA DGX Stations using vLLM. items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.one_liner: A developer used Claude Code to build an acoustic triangulation web app inspired by academic research to locate a mysterious beeping device.
items.summary: Faced with a mysterious, intermittently beeping device buried in a box room, software developer Simon Willison used Claude Code to build 'Beep Locator,' a software system that triangulates the source of acoustic signals using multiple commodity devices. Running on a Python web server with client interfaces connected via WebSockets, the app utilizes device-to-device audio ranging inspired by the 2007 research paper 'BeepBeep' by Chunyi Peng et al. By combining rough manual coordinate dragging with automated Fast Fourier Transform beep detection and interval measurement, the system successfully isolated the sound to within 40 centimeters, leading to an ancient carbon monoxide detector.
items.bottom_line: Claude Code can effectively build complex custom acoustic triangulation tools using commodity hardware to solve precise real-world localization problems.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: AI security scoping must align specific testing methodologies—from pen testing to red teaming—with concrete risk decisions across the full stack.
items.summary: Effective AI security scoping requires organizations to define the specific risk decision—such as shipping, gating, expanding, or mitigating—before selecting an appropriate evaluation method. Collapsing distinct practices like AI penetration testing, GenAI architecture security reviews, and AI red teaming into a generic 'AI check' leaves critical vulnerabilities unexamined. A robust assessment covers the full stack, including models, applications, APIs, RAG data pipelines, agents, tools, identity permissions, and third-party services, with testing depth scaling alongside system complexity.
items.bottom_line: Treating AI evaluations as a generic check leaves multi-layered enterprise AI deployments vulnerable; scoping must match specific risk decisions.

items.title: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have enabled state-of-the-art LLMs to be scaled to hundreds of billions of parameters, but they come with a fundamental and costly caveat: every expert MLP must occupy memory at inference time, even though the vast majority are idle for any given token. For example, Qwen3.5-122B has 256 experts in each of its 48 MoE layers, and 95% of its ~250 GB parameter memory footprint is taken up entirely by these expert MLPs alone. However, for any given token, only 8 experts in each layer are actually used. Expert pruning is one of the most direct fixes to this memory bottleneck. That is, permanently delete the least useful experts.

items.title: Bengaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat launched: How Indian Railways electrified the challenging Western Ghats route
items.one_liner: The new Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat service overcomes significant engineering hurdles in the Western Ghats to provide faster rail travel.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has launched the Vande Bharat Express service between Bengaluru and Madgaon, significantly improving connectivity to coastal Karnataka and Goa. The project required the complex electrification of the 55 km Sakleshpur-Subramanya Road Ghat section, which features a steep 1 in 50 gradient and 57 tunnels. This engineering feat involved specialized geological studies and the installation of 427 main brackets within tunnels to ensure stability against landslides and heavy rainfall. The new semi-high-speed train will serve 12 intermediate stations, benefiting tourists and business travelers in the region.
items.bottom_line: Electrification of the challenging Western Ghats route now enables semi-high-speed rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Goa's coastal hubs.
